title: The Convention Gap: Towards Measuring Implicit Communication in Cooperative AI Evaluation
one_sentence: A literal-information baseline exposes beyond-literal cooperation in Hanabi, without identifying how shared conventions formed.
problem: What does cooperative success reveal beyond explicitly conveyed information?
method: Retrospective replay of 100,956 Hanabi play actions; exact literal failure posterior minus observed failure; clustered uncertainty, within-participant comparisons and Off-Belief Learning validation.
findings: Gaps were +26.2 percentage points for human pairs, −0.7 for AI pairs and +16.4 for human–AI.
Controlled convention levels yielded increasing gaps; the Full–Intentional ordering did not replicate within participants.
biggest_weakness: Shared convention and unilateral adaptation remain observationally indistinguishable; prospective prediction is untested.
claim_boundary: Gap magnitude is not evidence of dyadic convention construction or causal history dependence.
why_researcher_should_care: Use a literal baseline alongside partner/history interventions; separate descriptive measurement from prediction.
evidence_notes: Full HTML v2 audited; independent quantitative audit agrees with diagnostic value and causal boundary.
Gap contains observed loss; contemporaneous association with loss cannot establish predictive validity.
